When the Mystics came close to forcing another shot-clock violation at the 5:11 mark, Jones pulled up from deep in the corner and drained a three to push New York’s lead to 54-43. By the end of the third, the Liberty had grabbed 18 rebounds and used a 19-5 run to go up 66-48.

Also, Connecticut forced a winner-take-all game because it again proved to be the better rebounding team. Center Jonquel Jones secured a game-high 13, besting the combined efforts of four Mystics starters. Of course, three of those players — Delle Donne, Kristi Toliver and Ariel Atkins — have played on despite injuries.

Jones hit a drop-step layup over Collier with 1:10 remaining as Collier was called for a foul. Jones hit the free throw to tie the game at 80 and set up the wild final moments. Friday marked one year to the day that the Liberty was heart- broken, losing a Game 4 at home that secured a title for the Las Vegas Aces.

And off-the-court issues weighed heavily on Jones’s mind. All she wanted to do was prove to the organization and its fans that she was the elite player the Liberty had traded for in January. “This year has probably been the most adversity that I’ve faced on the court and off the court, too,” said Jones, who declined to get into the off-court specifics.
